title: SSS configuration (sss.config.json, sss.local.json)
description: Everything lives in the section "Sss". Write only what you change. Keys are case-insensitive in SSS; this schema uses the spelling shown. Generated from the option classes; do not edit by hand.

Provider.description: "Citrix" for a real site, "Mock" for demo data (with a banner).

RefreshSeconds.description: Automatic refresh interval of the web interface in seconds.

StoreFrontUrl.description: Optional address of StoreFront; the UI then shows an "Open StoreFront" link (to start or reconnect sessions).

Auth.description: Authentication mode (IIS Windows authentication, or a fixed demo user in development).

Mode.description: "Iis" = Windows authentication of IIS (production). "Dev" = fixed demo user, only accepted when ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT=Development.

DevUserName.description: Development mode only: name of the fixed demo user.

DevUserSid.description: Development mode only: SID of the fixed demo user.

DevIsHelpdesk.description: Dev mode only: treat the demo user as a member of the helpdesk group.

DevRoles.description: Dev mode only: roles of the demo user, a list of L1, L2, L3, Auditor, Admin.

Audit.description: Audit trail: local files, retention and central destinations.

Directory.description: Directory for audit-YYYYMMDD.jsonl files; relative paths are based on the app directory.

PerServerFiles.description: Name the files audit-YYYYMMDD-SERVER.jsonl so several servers can write into one shared folder.

RetentionDays.description: Delete local audit and ops files older than this many days once every sink has passed them. 0 = keep.

OpsStream.description: Operational messages (warnings and errors of SSS itself) go into a second stream "ops" next to the audit trail.

Sinks.description: Central destinations. The local file is always written first; every sink gets a copy and catches up after an outage.

Unc.description: Destinations that copy the events to a shared folder.

Path.description: Shared folder (UNC path) the events are copied to: one file per day, server and stream.

Enabled.description: Set to false to switch this destination off without removing it.

Name.description: Name in the status page and for the position file; defaults to the sink type and number.

Include.description: Only events whose action starts with one of these (for example "helpdesk", "alert:"). Empty = all.

OnlyProblems.description: Only failures, rejections, alerts and operational problems (for a notification channel).

BatchSize.description: Maximum number of events sent in one batch.

Port.description: Port; 0 = the default of the protocol (514, or 6514 for TLS).

Format.description: Json (the record as it is) or Cef (Common Event Format).

AppName.description: Application name in the syslog header.

Framing.description: TCP/TLS framing: "Newline" (default of most collectors) or "OctetCount" (RFC 6587).

Enabled.description: Set to false to switch this destination off without removing it.

Name.description: Name in the status page and for the position file; defaults to the sink type and number.

Include.description: Only events whose action starts with one of these (for example "helpdesk", "alert:"). Empty = all.

OnlyProblems.description: Only failures, rejections, alerts and operational problems (for a notification channel).

BatchSize.description: Maximum number of events sent in one batch.

Http.description: HTTP(S) destinations (SIEM, log platforms, chat webhooks).

Url.description: Address that receives the events by POST; must be https:// unless AllowHttp is set.

Format.description: Ndjson, JsonArray, SplunkHec, ElasticBulk or Text (short sentences for chat webhooks).

Index.description: Elasticsearch/OpenSearch index for the bulk format.

AuthorizationFile.description: File whose content is the complete Authorization header value (for example "Splunk 1234-..." or "Bearer ..."), read for every request so the secret never sits in the configuration and can be rotated.

TimeoutSeconds.description: Time limit of one request in seconds.

AllowHttp.description: Allow plain http:// (otherwise the address must be https://).

Enabled.description: Set to false to switch this destination off without removing it.

Name.description: Name in the status page and for the position file; defaults to the sink type and number.

Include.description: Only events whose action starts with one of these (for example "helpdesk", "alert:"). Empty = all.

OnlyProblems.description: Only failures, rejections, alerts and operational problems (for a notification channel).

BatchSize.description: Maximum number of events sent in one batch.

Port.description: UDP port of the trap receiver.

Community.description: SNMP community string (sent in clear text: management network only).

EnterpriseOid.description: Your own enterprise OID, for example 1.3.6.1.4.1.NNNNN.1 (no default: pick the number your organisation owns).

Enabled.description: Set to false to switch this destination off without removing it.

Name.description: Name in the status page and for the position file; defaults to the sink type and number.

Include.description: Only events whose action starts with one of these (for example "helpdesk", "alert:"). Empty = all.

OnlyProblems.description: Only failures, rejections, alerts and operational problems (for a notification channel).

BatchSize.description: Maximum number of events sent in one batch.

Health.description: The anonymous health probe GET /healthz for load balancers.

Enabled.description: Serves GET /healthz (no details, 200 or 503) for load balancers. IIS must allow anonymous access to that path; scripts/install.ps1 -HealthEndpoint does that.

DataProtection.description: Shared key ring for several SSS servers.

KeyDirectory.description: Shared folder for the key ring when SSS runs on several servers (CSRF tokens then work on every server). Empty = keys stay on this server (single server, or a load balancer with sticky sessions).

ProtectToSid.description: Optional: encrypt the keys for this account or group SID (DPAPI-NG), e.g. the SID of the gMSA. Windows only.

RateLimit.description: Request limits per user and minute.

LogoffRequestsPerMinute.description: Log-off and end-process requests per user and minute.

ReadRequestsPerMinute.description: Listing sessions and CSV export; each call queries Citrix, so it is limited as well.

HelpdeskRequestsPerMinute.description: All helpdesk calls (search, overview, view, log-off) per helpdesk user.

Quality.description: Thresholds of the quality traffic lights.

RttWarnMs.description: ICA round-trip time in ms from which the light is yellow.

RttCritMs.description: ICA round-trip time in ms from which the light is red.

BandwidthWarnKbps.description: Available bandwidth in kbit/s at or below which the light is yellow.

BandwidthCritKbps.description: Available bandwidth in kbit/s at or below which the light is red.

LogonWarnSeconds.description: Logon duration in seconds from which the light is yellow.

LogonCritSeconds.description: Logon duration in seconds from which the light is red.

LoadWarn.description: Server load index from which the light is yellow.

LoadCrit.description: Server load index from which the light is red.

Citrix.description: Connection to the Citrix site (used when Provider is Citrix).

Controllers.description: Delivery Controller host names, tried in order (failover). With Discovery this may be empty or only a few names; the rest of the site is found automatically.

Discovery.description: Finds all Delivery Controllers of the site from one of them and keeps the list up to date.

Bootstrap.description: Controller to ask. Empty = the first entry of Controllers. If it is down, the cached and configured controllers are tried.

RefreshMinutes.description: How often the controller list is refreshed, in minutes.

AllowedSuffixes.description: Only controllers whose name ends with one of these suffixes are accepted (for example ".corp.local"). Empty = the domain part of the bootstrap controller. A manipulated answer can therefore not send requests elsewhere.

IncludeInactive.description: Also use controllers the Broker reports as not active (for example failed or in maintenance).

Balancing.description: How requests are spread over the controllers.

Strategy.description: "Failover" (default: the controller that answered last, the others as fallback), "RoundRobin" or "LeastLatency" (the faster of two random healthy controllers; spreads load and avoids slow ones).

Preferred.description: Controllers (or, if discovered, their zone) that are used first while they are healthy, for example the ones in the same data center.

FailureThreshold.description: A controller that failed this many times in a row is skipped for OpenSeconds.

OpenSeconds.description: How long a controller that keeps failing is skipped, in seconds.

PowerShellPath.description: Windows PowerShell 5.1 host that has the Citrix snap-ins (or the Remote PowerShell SDK) installed.

WorkerScript.description: Defaults to Citrix/sss-broker-worker.ps1 next to the application.

SnapinOverride.description: Test hook: a script that is dot-sourced instead of loading the Citrix snap-in (provides fake cmdlets).

Workers.description: Number of warm PowerShell workers (each holds one loaded snap-in, roughly 60-100 MB).

RequestTimeoutSeconds.description: Time limit of one Broker or Monitor request in seconds.

Cloud.description: Citrix Cloud (DaaS) instead of an on-premises site: read-only, through the Monitor service in the cloud.

Enabled.description: Use Citrix Cloud (DaaS) instead of Delivery Controllers: read-only, no snap-in and no VDA access.

CustomerId.description: Customer id of the Citrix Cloud account (shown with the API clients).

ClientId.description: Id of a Citrix Cloud API client (Identity and Access Management > API access). Give it the least rights that allow reading the Monitor data.

ApiBase.description: Overrides the address derived from the region (testing); an https:// address without a trailing path.

Monitor.description: History, quality data and the expert view (Monitor OData).

Enabled.description: Set to false to run without history and metrics (live sessions and log-off only).

BaseUrls.description: One Monitor address per Delivery Controller, tried in order (failover). Empty = derived from Controllers.

UseHttps.description: Scheme of the default address when BaseUrl is empty. Set to false only for a controller without an HTTPS binding.

MetricsDateField.description: Property of SessionMetrics used to pick the newest sample. Verify with scripts/Test-SssCitrix.ps1.

IcaRttField.description: Property of SessionMetrics holding the ICA round-trip time in ms.

BandwidthField.description: Property of SessionMetrics with the bandwidth available towards the client. Seen on CVAD 2507: OutputBandwidthAvailable = 105379594 on a 100 Mbit/s LAN, i.e. bits per second.

BandwidthDivisor.description: Converts the bandwidth field to kbit/s (1000 for bit/s).

MaxPages.description: Maximum number of pages read for one history query.

ClientVersionField.description: Property of Connection with the Workspace app version. Used when the site delivers it (checked in $metadata).

ClientPlatformField.description: Property of Connection with the client platform (Windows, Mac, iOS ...). Used when the site delivers it.

Processes.description: Ending processes and profile analysis through the JEA endpoint on the VDAs.

Enabled.description: Turn process control and profile analysis on (needs the JEA endpoint on the VDAs).

Configuration.description: Name of the JEA session configuration on the VDAs.

Audience.description: "All" = users for their own sessions and the helpdesk; "Helpdesk" = helpdesk only.

TimeoutSeconds.description: Connecting to a VDA takes longer than a Broker call, so process requests get their own time limit.

ProfileInfo.description: Shows the profile type and size in the expert view (the "Get-SssProfile" command of the JEA endpoint).

ProfileScanSeconds.description: Time limit of the profile folder scan on the VDA; 0 = type only, no size.

Helpdesk.description: Helpdesk behaviour: group, ticket requirement, limits.

Group.description: AD group whose members have all helpdesk rights (level 3), e.g. CORP\SSS-Helpdesk. Kept for existing installations; Sss:Roles allows finer levels. Empty = not used. Resolved to a SID at startup.

ReasonRequired.description: Require a ticket number or reason for every helpdesk action that changes something or reads processes or profiles (log-off, message, end process). Free text; the content is not checked, it is written to the audit log. Off by default: the field stays available and is logged when filled in.

BulkAlertThreshold.description: A helpdesk request that logs off this many sessions or more is reported as an alert event (audit sinks can notify).

MaxSessions.description: Upper limit for the farm-wide session overview.

MessageTitle.description: Title of messages the helpdesk sends to a session.

Roles.description: AD groups for the helpdesk levels and the auditor and admin roles.

Level1Group.description: Looks at users, sessions and the expert view; changes nothing.

Level2Group.description: Level 1 plus: log off sessions and send messages.

Level3Group.description: Level 2 plus: processes and profile of other users, end processes.

AuditorGroup.description: Reads the audit trail and its evaluation. Not part of any helpdesk level.

AdminGroup.description: Status, controllers and the list of SSS servers. Empty = every helpdesk member (as before roles existed).

Instances.description: Server list for several SSS servers (shared folder).

Directory.description: Shared folder (for example \\fs01\sss-state) that every SSS server can write. Empty = single server, feature off.

Expected.description: The names of all SSS servers (computer names). A listed server that does not report is shown as missing, a reporting server that is not listed as unexpected. Empty = no completeness check, the servers that report are the list.

HeartbeatSeconds.description: How often this server reports to the shared folder, in seconds.

StaleSeconds.description: A server that has not reported for this long counts as not running.

Enabled.description: Serve GET /metrics (Prometheus text format, no personal data).

AllowedIps.description: Addresses or networks (for example 10.0.5.0/24) that may read the metrics. Empty = only the server itself.

Environment.description: The Environment view (client versions, locations) and the outdated-client hint.

Locations.description: Your sites or offices, each with the networks (CIDR or single address) its clients connect from.

Name.description: Name shown in the Environment tab, for example the office or data center.

Networks.description: Networks of this location, for example 10.20.0.0/16. The most specific match wins.

MinClientVersion.description: Oldest acceptable Workspace app version per platform, for example {"Windows": "26.3.0", "Mac": "26.3.0"}; "*" applies to every other platform. Clients below it are counted as outdated in the Environment tab and their users get a hint. Empty = no check.

HintOutdatedClient.description: Show the user a hint in the session list when the own Workspace app is below the minimum version.

DataDirectory.description: Folder for state SSS keeps between restarts (forwarding positions, controller cache, drain flag). Relative paths are based on the app directory; the app pool identity needs write access.

PathBase.description: Application path for local runs behind a prefix. Behind IIS the ASP.NET Core Module sets it; leave it empty.
